faq.question: Does strong Achievement Striving guarantee success?

faq.answer: It may reflect selective priorities, sufficiency, or noncompetitive goals. Conduct and chosen aims need direct examination.
faq.question: Does weaker Achievement Striving mean lacking ambition or growth?

faq.answer: High standards can exist without rigid error concerns or self-worth dependence. A facet does not diagnose perfectionism.
faq.question: How is Achievement Striving different from perfectionism?

faq.answer: Goals and habits can change. This page does not forecast a stable score trajectory.
faq.question: Can this tendency change?

faq.answer: Ask what support is wanted, respect autonomy, notice recovery needs, and avoid making output the only measure of the relationship.

sections.body:
Achievement Striving concerns attraction to demanding goals, improvement, and standards that require sustained effort. It describes motivational direction—not success, worth, talent, productivity, income, or whether a goal deserves pursuit.

“Achievement Striving within Conscientiousness: drive toward demanding goals and standards” is used on this page as a descriptive construct within the NEO/IPIP-NEO 30-facet framework. The official IPIP resource describes scales that measure constructs similar to NEO facets and lists item mappings ([S11](https://ipip.ori.org/Finding_Scales_to_Measure_Particular_Constructs.htm)); this does not make scores from different instruments, translations, or products interchangeable.

FermatMind has not published product-level reliability, validity, Chinese norms, or individual predictive evidence for the score discussed on this page. This material is for self-observation and education. It is not for clinical diagnosis, hiring screening, school admission, or replacing a career decision.

> **Content method and update:** FermatMind Editorial prepared this page with AI-assisted drafting and checked terminology, boundaries, and evidence against public personality-psychology sources. It is for self-understanding and education; it is not clinical diagnosis, hiring screening, or individual-outcome prediction. Substantive update: 2026-07-19; review mode: solo_operator; not clinically reviewed.
sections.heading: Evidence and Interpretation Boundaries

sections.body: A stronger tendency may set ambitious targets and experience progress as energizing. A weaker tendency may prefer “good enough,” protect nonwork priorities, or invest deeply only in selected goals. Outcomes also depend on skill, health, opportunity, resources, discrimination, and goal quality.
sections.heading: Precise Definition

sections.body: Achievement Striving belongs to [Conscientiousness](/en/personality/big-five/conscientiousness), where standards can organize effort over time.
sections.heading: Parent Domain

sections.body:
- **Achievement Striving versus Self-Discipline:** Ambition chooses a demanding destination; [Self-Discipline](/en/personality/big-five/facets/self-discipline) helps continue unpleasant steps.
- **Achievement Striving versus Competence:** [Competence](/en/personality/big-five/facets/competence) concerns expected capability, not desired level of accomplishment.
- **Achievement Striving versus perfectionism:** Perfectionism can involve rigid error concerns and self-worth contingencies. A facet score cannot establish it.
sections.heading: Distinguishing Neighboring Facets

sections.body: A stronger tendency may appear as stretch goals, tracking progress, seeking challenge, or difficulty resting without accomplishment. A weaker tendency may appear as bounded goals, stable satisfaction, selective effort, or declining status competition. Economic pressure and role demands can mimic ambition.
sections.heading: Behavioral Cues

sections.body: Someone may strive intensely in art but not career hierarchy, or at work but not sport. Burnout, illness, caregiving, and blocked opportunity alter visible pursuit. Compare chosen standards across meaningful domains.
sections.heading: Contextual Differences

sections.body:
- Setting a target beyond minimum requirements.
- Seeking feedback that supports improvement.
- Linking time to measurable progress.
- Escalating standards after success.
- Neglecting recovery or relationships when goals dominate.
sections.heading: Possible Expressions When Stronger

sections.body:
- Defining sufficiency and stopping there.
- Preserving leisure, relationships, or stability over status.
- Avoiding externally imposed competition.
- Underinvesting when a meaningful opportunity needs sustained stretch.
- Choosing depth or care without public achievement markers.
sections.heading: Possible Expressions When Weaker

sections.body: Stronger Achievement Striving can support sustained development and challenging projects. Possible costs include overwork, chronic dissatisfaction, narrow identity, and pursuing a harmful metric. Weaker Achievement Striving can protect balance and contentment; possible costs include missed opportunities or underdeveloped goals. Neither level ranks a life.
sections.heading: Strengths and Costs

sections.body: A researcher sets demanding publication goals but also defines nonnegotiable sleep and family time. Ambition structures work without becoming a total identity. Success still depends on many factors beyond the facet.
sections.heading: An Original Case

sections.body: A skilled craftsperson rejects promotion, maintains a modest workload, and produces excellent work. Low interest in status and stretch targets does not mean low ability, care, or growth.
sections.heading: An Original Counterexample

sections.body:
1. Who chose your most demanding current standard?
2. Does progress energize you, relieve anxiety, or protect self-worth?
3. What would “enough” look like?
4. Which goal deserves greater effort, and which should be retired?
5. What costs rise when the target escalates?
sections.heading: Self-Observation Questions

sections.body: Select one goal and write its purpose, minimum useful outcome, stretch outcome, and stop rule. Track effort and recovery for seven days. The experiment tests goal design, not personal value.
sections.heading: Low-Risk Action Experiment

sections.body: Return to [Conscientiousness](/en/personality/big-five/conscientiousness) or the [30-facet guide](/en/personality/big-five/facets). Continue with [Competence](/en/personality/big-five/facets/competence), [Order](/en/personality/big-five/facets/order), [Dutifulness](/en/personality/big-five/facets/dutifulness), [Self-Discipline](/en/personality/big-five/facets/self-discipline), [Deliberation](/en/personality/big-five/facets/deliberation).
